title: USB 3.0 Interceptor And Future Router Relay
objective: Define and implement one two-way transport contract that begins as a USB 3.0 file-backed interceptor/spool and can later be promoted to an authenticated private-LAN router relay without creating a second LeafOS authority.
constraints: The USB phase is a file-backed interceptor and durable spool, not a transparent packet router.
The future router phase supplies LAN connectivity but never becomes a LeafOS scheduler or execution authority.
All mutation requests enter through the existing typed loop inlet and retain approval, work-order, path, and validation policy.
No arbitrary shell, provider, PowerShell, Bash, Python, or model-control payloads may cross the transport boundary.
No WAN exposure, port forwarding, UPnP, cloud relay, credentials, model weights, or private chain-of-thought on the transport medium.
Historical run evidence and durable leafos.* objects remain readable and are never rewritten by transport delivery.

deliverables: explicit USB root and stable identity contract
atomic publication, hash, deduplication, expiry, acknowledgement, and rejection handling
fixture tests for interruption, safe removal, replay, and out-of-order delivery
disabled-by-default router relay with no WAN path

acceptance: Valid USB requests reach the existing loop inlet exactly once.
Valid results and monitor snapshots return through the USB outbox.
Malformed, unauthorized, expired, replayed, partial, and hash-invalid messages are rejected without queue mutation.
USB removal and reconnection are resumable and do not duplicate accepted tasks.
USB and future LAN adapters produce equivalent inlet inputs and audit evidence.
The existing monitor, TUI, queue, journal, checkpoint, report, and resident supervisor remain the only authorities.
The future LAN relay is authenticated, encrypted, private-LAN-only, and disabled by default.
